response.prediction: Surgeons prevent major blood loss during coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) by using several careful techniques. Before starting the surgery, they often connect the patient to a heart-lung machine, which takes over the function of the heart and lungs, allowing the blood to be oxygenated and the heart to be stopped. This gives the surgeon a still, bloodless field to work in. The surgeon also uses special instruments to clamp the blood vessels and carefully sews the grafts in place to avoid damaging the vessels. Additionally, the surgical team uses medications to thin the blood just enough to help it flow smoothly, and they closely monitor the patient’s blood pressure and fluid levels throughout the procedure. These steps together help keep blood loss to a minimum during the surgery.
